title: How this summer’s heat and drought impacted crops in Europe – in six charts - Carbon Brief
gist: Europe's 2026 summer heat, drought and wildfires cut EU cereal production by roughly 9% and pushed France's maize output to a four-decade low, with the June heatwave alone causing an estimated €2-2.3bn in grain losses and the UK on track for one of its worst harvests since 1984.

insights.claim: French cereal (wheat, barley, oats) production is expected to drop by almost 8 megatonnes in 2026 compared with 2025, the largest absolute decline of any EU country.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: France is the EU's largest agricultural producer, so an 8Mt shortfall there disproportionately drives bloc-wide grain supply and price dynamics.
insights.quote: French cereal production is expected to drop by almost 8 megatonnes (Mt) in 2026, compared to 2025.

insights.claim: Germany faces the second-largest EU cereal production loss in 2026, down almost 4 megatonnes versus 2025, driven by a long dry period combined with record heatwaves.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Confirms the shock is concentrated in the EU's two largest agricultural economies, amplifying bloc-wide supply tightness rather than being diffused evenly.

insights.claim: Almost all European countries analysed by the European Commission (26 of 27, excluding Malta for data reasons) will see cereal production declines in 2026 versus 2025, with Bulgaria the only exception.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A near-universal continental decline signals a systemic weather-driven supply shock rather than a localized or idiosyncratic one, raising the odds of sustained EU grain price pressure.

insights.claim: Overall EU cereal production is projected to fall 9% in 2026 versus 2025, with only one year in the past decade (2024) recording a lower output level.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A top-of-decade production shortfall points to tighter EU grain export availability and likely upward pressure on regional and global grain prices into 2026-27.
insights.quote: Cereal production is set to fall by 9% compared to 2025, according to the European Commission.

insights.claim: EU maize production is projected to drop 13% to 52 megatonnes in 2026, the lowest EU maize output level since 2007.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Maize is a key livestock feedstock, so a near two-decade-low harvest signals knock-on cost pressure for European meat and dairy producers.

themes.theme: Yield divergence and the limits of adaptation

insights.claim: The EU Joint Research Centre's bulletin found heat and water scarcity had 'substantially worsened' crop expectations across western and most of central Europe in summer 2026, with local crop failures 'likely' in France, southern Germany, northern and central Italy, and Hungary.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: An official EU body flagging 'likely' crop failures (not just reduced yields) across multiple major producers is a stronger signal than typical seasonal variability and warrants monitoring for further downgrades.
insights.quote: significantly reduced”, with local crop failures “likely” in areas such as France, southern Germany, northern and central Italy, and Hungary

insights.claim: Slovakia, Austria and Hungary are expected to see the largest cereal yield declines in the EU for 2026, each falling by more than one tonne per hectare versus 2025.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Identifies the specific Central European producers most exposed to further downside if the drought pattern recurs or intensifies.

insights.claim: Portugal was the only EU country to see cereal yields increase in 2026, because irrigated crops performed well while rain-fed crops elsewhere showed growing heat stress.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Irrigation infrastructure is emerging as the key differentiator between resilient and failing harvests, favoring agtech and irrigation-equipment investment in exposed regions.

insights.claim: A German cropping-systems expert argues there is 'no one-fits-all solution' for climate adaptation because farming must cope with both heat/drought and prolonged wet periods, not just one extreme.
insights.speaker: Prof Til Feike (Julius Kühn-Institut), via Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Signals that single-solution adaptation bets (e.g., drought-only irrigation buildouts) may be insufficient; diversified, multi-hazard resilience investment is the more durable thesis.
insights.quote: In the long run, farming must adapt better to more extreme weather conditions, not only heat and drought, but also prolonged wet periods. So, there is no one-fits-all solution for climate change adaptation.

themes.theme: The economic bill for the June heatwave

insights.claim: The record June 2026 heatwave contributed to an estimated €2-2.3bn in cumulative EU grain production losses, per ECIU analysis of Coceral trader-association forecasts between June and July.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Gives investors a concrete euro figure for single-event weather risk to European grain markets, useful for calibrating crop-insurance and commodity-hedging exposure.

insights.claim: France, Germany, Hungary and Spain together accounted for 86% of the revenue lost from the June heatwave's grain damage.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Highlights concentration risk: EU grain supply shocks are disproportionately a function of weather in just four countries, making their harvest data the highest-signal indicators to track.

insights.claim: A rapid climate attribution study found the intense June 2026 heat in western Europe would have been 'virtually impossible' just 50 years ago, and it was the region's hottest June on record.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Quantified attribution strengthens the case that agricultural weather risk in Europe is structurally shifting, not reverting to historical baselines, supporting a secular re-rating of ag-weather risk premia.

insights.claim: Triodos Bank estimates this summer's extreme weather could cut EU GDP by around 1% (roughly €180bn) in 2026.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A single-summer, ~1%-of-GDP macro hit reframes extreme heat as a macroeconomic risk factor for the EU, not merely a sectoral agriculture story.

insights.claim: If current trends hold, average UK cereal and oilseed yields will produce the UK's worst harvest since detailed records began in 1984.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A record-worst UK harvest points to sustained upward pressure on UK food import demand and retail food prices through 2026-27.

insights.claim: 2026 UK harvest surveys show barley yields falling 15%, oats 14% and wheat 6% year-on-year, per the Agriculture and Horticulture Development Board.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Gives crop-specific magnitudes for UK feed and food-grain supply tightening, relevant to UK food, brewing and livestock-feed input costs.

insights.claim: Four of the UK's five worst harvests on record have occurred within the past decade, according to ECIU, indicating an accelerating frequency of severe harvest years.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A clustering of extreme-harvest years in the last ten years is a stronger investable signal of structural climate risk to UK agriculture than any single bad year.

insights.claim: The chairman of UK produce distributor Nationwide Produce told BBC News that consumers will likely see higher prices and/or smaller vegetables in supermarkets as a result of the poor harvest.
insights.speaker: Tim O'Malley (Nationwide Produce), via Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Direct read-through to UK grocery retail and food-inflation trackers for the remainder of 2026.

insights.claim: French maize production is set to fall more than one-third (35%) year-on-year in 2026, which could make it France's lowest maize harvest since 1980.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A 45-year-low in the EU's top agricultural producer's maize output is a material input-cost shock for European livestock feed and food-processing supply chains.

insights.claim: France recorded more than 7,300 excess deaths during summer 2026 heatwaves alongside a record number of weather stations exceeding 40C.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Frames the agricultural losses within a broader human and public-health toll, relevant to healthcare-system cost and labor-productivity impact assessments.

insights.claim: Record-early grape harvests recorded across France since mid-July are producing smaller, less juicy grapes that will yield less wine, per Le Monde.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Signals a coming reduction in French wine volumes, relevant to wine producers, exporters and related commodity/luxury-goods supply chains.
insights.quote: smaller, less juicy grapes, which will yield less wine

insights.claim: Global food prices are at their highest level since early 2023, driven by heatwaves and energy price dynamics, according to the UN Food and Agriculture Organization.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Anchors the European crop story within a global food-inflation cycle, relevant to agricultural commodity and consumer-staples positioning.

insights.claim: Blocked fertiliser supplies through the Strait of Hormuz and elevated fuel costs are additional factors weighing on this year's European agricultural output, compounding the direct weather damage.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Links a geopolitical chokepoint disruption directly to European farm input costs and yields, indicating that resolution of the Hormuz crisis would be a tailwind for 2027 harvest prospects.
